title: The Provision of Devil's Throat
premise: Emrys Marchetti, a riverboat captain who has spent fifteen years making herself unremarkable on the Verrazano River, is hired to resupply the Halvorsen expedition surveying the Devil's Throat gorge for a mining concession. When she arrives, the camp is abandoned except for one survivor who refuses to speak of what they found in the caves—a discovery that could make or ruin everyone holding permits. As the concession deadline looms and corporate fixers close in from downriver, Emrys must choose between delivering the truth, destroying it, or carrying it home herself. She brings the survivor back alive, burns the survey records at the Throat's edge, and finally claims her own name and history on the river she once used to hide.
about_author: Bram Fairweather is the pen name of a former deckhand turned novelist who spent six seasons working freight runs on remote interior rivers. Their fiction draws on the river towns, salvage crews, and half-legal expeditions they witnessed firsthand.

chapters.title: The Mood of the Water
chapters.summary: Emrys navigates her aging boat, the Kestrel, through low-water season, establishing her careful invisibility—no debts, no questions, no past. A telegram offers triple pay to run supplies upriver to the Halvorsen survey camp above Devil's Throat. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: wary temptation; money like this means someone is desperate, and desperation travels upstream.

chapters.title: Manifest of Strangers
chapters.summary: Emrys loads cargo and meets the client's representative, Odile Vance, whose permit paperwork doesn't quite match the company letterhead. Emrys notices but says nothing—her survival depends on not noticing. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: quiet unease; she recognizes the smell of a deal going bad because she grew up inside one.

chapters.title: Dead Air Above the Gorge
chapters.summary: The Kestrel fights the rapids toward Devil's Throat while radio calls to the Halvorsen camp go unanswered. Emrys finds the landing burned, tents slashed from the inside, and one man alive: surveyor Tomas Reyes, dehydrated and mute, clutching a sealed brass canister. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: dread hardening into resolve; the wilderness forgives nothing, and neither will whoever did this.

chapters.title: What the Caves Kept
chapters.summary: Tomas begins speaking in fragments: the expedition found something in the limestone galleries—ore, yes, but also evidence the vein was already claimed, worked, and hidden by people the maps say never lived there. The crew split over whether to report it; the argument ended violently. POV: Emrys with Tomas's recounted memories. Emotional beat: the weight of knowledge as burden rather than prize.

chapters.title: Downstream Traffic
chapters.summary: Emrys spots another boat working the narrows below—not salvage, not patrol. Vance's employers have sent their own people to secure the site before the permits expire in nine days. Emrys hides the Kestrel in a side slough and realizes she is now the only witness between two armed crews. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: hunted stillness; invisibility was never really an option.

chapters.title: The Price of Silence
chapters.summary: Vance catches up and makes an offer: deliver the canister quietly and both their names stay clean. She reveals she knows Emrys's real surname—the one tied to a wrecked boat and drowned men years ago. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: the past surfacing like a snagged hull; belonging bought with silence costs more than she thought.

chapters.title: Nine Days to Expiry
chapters.summary: Emrys runs the Kestrel through night water to reach the land office ahead of the rival crew, testing every sandbar by feel. Tomas, recovering his voice, insists the find belongs to the river communities, not the companies—but reporting it dooms them all to litigation and worse. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: momentum and doubt braided together; speed feels like honesty.

chapters.title: Ambush at Split Rock
chapters.summary: The rival crew boards the Kestrel at the narrows. In a brutal close-quarters fight among the cargo, Emrys scuttles nothing but lets the current take the canister overboard into Devil's Throat itself—unreachable, unrecoverable. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: climax; choosing destruction over delivery, and owning the cost.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: With the evidence gone, Vance's leverage collapses; the permits lapse worthless, and the rival crew withdraws. Emrys gives a statement to the river magistrate—her full name, her father's wreck, everything—finding that truth spoken aloud weighs less than truth hoarded. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: release; memory stops being a debt and becomes a rudder.

chapters.title: Home Water
chapters.summary: Emrys and Tomas take the Kestrel back downriver as the season turns. She signs on to ferry mail and medicine to the villages above the Throat—the people the cave records would have erased—and paints her true name on the hull. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not inherited; the river remembers, and so will she.
